competency_questions: How many papers directly compare a retrieval augmentation method and a fine-tuning method on the same benchmark?
List the papers that test both approaches, with the benchmark and each approach's reported score.
Among the directly comparing papers, how many found fine-tuning superior and how many found retrieval augmentation superior, and are there any ties?
briefs.definition: The number of papers in the corpus that evaluate both retrieval augmentation and fine-tuning on the same task or benchmark to enable a direct comparison.

measure.filter: paper evaluates both retrieval augmentation and fine-tuning on a shared benchmark or task

needs: Method names or families indicating retrieval augmentation (e.g., RAG, retrieval-augmented generation) as evaluated in the paper
Method names or families indicating fine-tuning (e.g., supervised fine-tuning, LoRA, parameter-efficient fine-tuning) as evaluated in the paper
The shared benchmark or task and the reported performance metric for each approach

scope.papers: all papers in the corpus that report empirical results for at least one retrieval augmentation method and at least one fine-tuning method on a comparable evaluation

briefs.title: Direct head-to-head evaluation papers

competency_questions: Which approach, retrieval augmentation or fine-tuning, is reported as the best-performing method in more papers?
For each approach, how many papers report it as the winner on its primary task, and which paper is a representative example?
Does any paper report both approaches and declare a tie, and if so, how is that tie counted in this ranking?
briefs.definition: A ranking of approaches (retrieval augmentation versus fine-tuning) by the number of papers in which each is reported as the best-performing method on the paper's primary task.
needs: Identification of the paper's primary task and its best-performing method
Classification of that best method as retrieval augmentation, fine-tuning, or neither
The reported metric value supporting the best-performing claim

scope.papers: all papers in the corpus that report a primary empirical result for at least one of retrieval augmentation or fine-tuning, where the paper's own conclusion or best-reported setting identifies a winning approach

briefs.title: Best-performing approach per paper

competency_questions: Across the corpus, which approach has the higher mean reported metric, and by how much?
How many papers contribute a measurable score to each approach's mean?
If a paper reports scores on multiple benchmarks, how is it counted so that each paper contributes at most once to the aggregate?
briefs.definition: A comparison of the mean reported performance metric of retrieval augmentation methods versus fine-tuning methods across all papers in the corpus, weighted so that each paper contributes once.
needs: A numeric performance metric (e.g., accuracy, F1, BLEU) for each reported method
The benchmark or task name associated with each reported metric
Classification of each method as retrieval augmentation or fine-tuning

scope.papers: all papers in the corpus that report a numeric performance metric for at least one retrieval augmentation method and/or at least one fine-tuning method on a named benchmark

briefs.title: Aggregate performance comparison

question: Is retrieval augmentation or fine-tuning the better approach according to this corpus?
